annotation.title_clean: Interplay between the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) & In vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation (IVDR) and the Artificial Intelligence Act (AIA)
annotation.title_en: Interplay between the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) & In vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation (IVDR) and the Artificial Intelligence Act (AIA)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Artificial Intelligence Board (AIB) and Medical Device Coordination Group (MDCG)
annotation.summary_en: Joint AI Board and MDCG FAQ guidance (June 2025) explaining how the EU AI Act applies alongside the MDR and IVDR to AI-enabled medical devices. It covers high-risk classification, data governance, transparency, human oversight, robustness, conformity assessment, substantial modification and post-market monitoring, and encourages integrating procedures. It is non-binding.
key_provisions_or_claims: Medical device AI is high-risk under AIA Art. 6(1) if it is a safety component or a device and needs third-party notified body assessment under MDR/IVDR.
MDR/IVDR and AIA apply simultaneously and complementarily; manufacturers are 'providers'.
Manufacturers are encouraged to integrate AIA testing, documentation and reporting into existing MDR/IVDR procedures under AIA Art. 8(2).
Transparency, human oversight, data governance, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements are mapped to MDR/IVDR obligations.
Document is non-binding and not an official Commission position; further horizontal guidelines are forthcoming.
